title: E-scooter rental at Sun Moon Lake: proof that the visitor is still lawfully in the country for the rental period
moment: A foreign visitor rents a shared e-scooter or a rental e-scooter from a small shop at a tourist spot. The shop photographs the passport and the home-country driving permit or International Driving Permit, mainly to be able to chase the renter for fines or damage, and needs to know the visitor is not about to leave the country before the bike is returned.
verifier: Rental shop owner or the scooter-sharing app's onboarding flow
predicate: Holder's lawful stay does not end before the planned return time plus a grace period, and holds a driving authorization valid for a light scooter in Taiwan, shown as two time-bounded claims with no passport details.
disclosed_today: Passport photo page image, entry stamp, driving permit image, often a phone number and hotel name; stored on the shop owner's phone and in chat apps.
issuer: National Immigration Agency for the stay claim; Ministry of Transportation and Communications (Directorate General of Highways / motor vehicle office) for the driving-authorization claim
why_zk: The shop's real risk is unrecoverable loss if the renter leaves Taiwan, so the stay-end bound and a driving-authorization flag address it directly without keeping passport images on a shop owner's personal phone. Weakness: the shop also wants a deposit and a way to chase the person, and a pure predicate proof does not provide a contact for debt recovery; the deposit on a payment card would still do that job, and the claim only removes the identity-document photo, not the commercial risk.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In tw-gov-household-register-proxy-copy-discretion, how many document copies get collected is left to the office's own discretion; here, the shop owner's habit of photographing everything plays that role of unbounded discretion that a fixed predicate proof would cap.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A government office that holds a record may ask a proxy's requester for a copy of the principal's identity document, and the scope of what it may collect is left to the office's discretion. | mechanism: None stated; collection of document copies left to agency discretion under PDPA and administrative procedure rules.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In an-b-attorney-client, protection collapses when an unnecessary third party is in the room; here, the owner's personal phone and chat groups holding the passport photo play that role of the outside party, which the proof removes.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A party must consult an advisor about a sensitive matter without the advisor, or anyone else, learning or revealing more than the matter requires, but the protection breaks as soon as an outsider is in the room unless the outsider is essential to the relationship. | mechanism: Evidentiary privilege over communications, lost by third-party presence except essential agents such as interpreters; no technical mechanism.

title: Temple-run relief kitchen and clinic corner: same nurse, many one-off deployments, no cross-event trail
moment: A community development association in Hualien organises a weekend relief point after an earthquake, with a blood-pressure and wound-care corner staffed by volunteer nurses recruited via Facebook and LINE. Several of the same nurses also volunteer at the Tzu Chi, Red Cross and township stations the same week. Each organiser wants to confirm the licence is in good standing before letting someone touch residents' medical items.
verifier: Community association (社區發展協會) volunteer team lead running the relief point
predicate: Presenter holds a nursing licence in good standing, status refreshed within the past 7 days, shown through an unlinkable presentation so that the same nurse showing it at two relief points cannot be matched by the organisers.
disclosed_today: Each organiser asks for a licence photo and ID card photo in a group chat, so the same nurse's full identity and licence number are scattered across several unrelated groups run by different civic bodies, each with its own unknown retention.
issuer: Taiwan Nurses Association together with the MOHW registry, issuing a licence-status credential into the holder's wallet, refreshed by the registry on each renewal cycle
why_zk: The benefit is unlinkability across events: if each presentation is the same signed licence number, organisers can still collude or leak and track one nurse across sites, like a third-party cookie. Unlinkable proofs give each organiser only 'in good standing'. Weakness: a small relief team often knows the nurse personally and informal trust is fast, so the wallet flow is extra friction for volunteers who just show up; and the 7-day window depends on registry freshness that may not exist yet.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In an-a-samesite-cookies, a stored credential sent in every context lets third parties recognise the same browser across sites, and SameSite limits it to the issuing context; here, the licence number attached to every relief-point request plays that role, and a per-verifier unlinkable presentation limits it to one event.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A stored credential should be presented only to the party that issued it in the current context, but the browser sends it on any request the context triggers, so an unrelated observer can match the holder across contexts. | mechanism: The SameSite cookie attribute, which limits the cookie to same-site requests (Strict, Lax, or None); the IETF draft describes it as a per-cookie setting, and cross-site behaviour depends on the chosen value.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In tw-platform-gym-id-card-copies-interp, a gym asks for full front-and-back ID and card copies when a narrower check might do and the regulator leaves necessity to case-by-case review; here, the relief-point lead asking for ID and licence photos plays that role, with the 'in good standing' proof as the unnamed less-intrusive alternative.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A service provider signing up a customer must check identity and payment, but it asks for full front-and-back copies of identity and card documents, and the regulator leaves whether that exceeds the purpose to case-by-case fact-finding. | mechanism: None stated; the letter says less-intrusive alternatives must be considered but names none.

title: Landlord-less sublet: a flat's current tenants screen an incoming roommate without seeing a document
moment: Three university graduates in Tainan in a shared flat need a fourth to take over a room in two weeks. A candidate who answers the listing is asked to email a scan of their ID, criminal record certificate and student card to all three tenants, and the tenants forward it between themselves on a messaging app to decide.
verifier: The three existing tenants, as a peer group choosing a new roommate
predicate: The candidate is not on the violent-offender list as of the current list root, shown separately to each tenant with a fresh presentation so tenants cannot collude to link them
disclosed_today: Scans of ID card, criminal record certificate and student card, forwarded among three tenants and stored in their chat histories
issuer: A community-run issuer is unrealistic; the practical issuer is the National Police Agency or a licensed intermediary (e.g. the roommate platform's identity partner) holding a delegated signing key for a police-published list root
why_zk: Each tenant needs only the not-on-list bit, yet document scans end up in four private chat histories with no deletion duty, since private individuals fall outside the real enforcement reach of the PDPA's household exception. Per-verifier presentations hide the candidate's identity from tenants who then reject them, which today leaves a rejected person's documents circulating. Weakness: the PDPA's household-use exception means no one is legally compelled to minimise, so adoption relies entirely on the platform or wallet making the proof easier than sending a scan; and a landlord or school would still ask for a student card, which this proof does not replace.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In tw-gov-household-register-proxy-copy-discretion, the office may ask for copies of identity documents at its own discretion with no stated limit; here, each of the three tenants plays that role, deciding for themselves what scans to demand, and the proof replaces that open discretion with a fixed single predicate.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A government office that holds a record may ask a proxy's requester for a copy of the principal's identity document, and the scope of what it may collect is left to the office's discretion. | mechanism: None stated; collection of document copies left to agency discretion under PDPA and administrative procedure rules.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In an-a-tor-onion, no single relay holds both origin identity and final destination; here, the issuer, the presenting wallet and each tenant each see only their own layer (list root, proof, a one-time presentation), so none holds both the candidate's identity and the full screening outcome.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A route must be relayed through intermediaries so that no single intermediary holds both the origin identity and the final destination, while the traffic still reaches the endpoint. | mechanism: Onion routing, where the message is wrapped in one encryption layer per relay, and each relay peels only its own layer and passes the rest to the next hop.

title: Hot-spring hotel front desk: tattoo-policy age or women's-bath eligibility without ID photo
moment: A family checks into a hot-spring hotel in Beitou. The desk clerk wants to confirm the guests may use the women's bath and, for a guest with visible tattoos, whether the guest meets the venue's tattoo-policy age. Today the clerk photocopies or photographs the national ID card and logs it on a paper sheet kept at the counter.
verifier: Front desk of a Beitou hot-spring hotel (private operator)
predicate: Holder is registered female in the household register OR holder's age is at or above the venue's tattoo-policy threshold (membership in the set of eligible persons); nothing else is revealed
disclosed_today: Full national ID card copy or photo: name, ID number, birth date, address, household-register details, photo
issuer: Ministry of the Interior household registration offices, through the Taiwan digital wallet (TW FidO) credential
why_zk: The venue collects the ID copy out of habit and fraud screening, with no legal duty, so a one-bit OR claim removes the whole copy. Weakness: gender is binary in the register, so the claim says nothing for trans or non-binary guests, who may still be challenged by staff, and a guest whose phone is dead falls back to the old copy. Staff may also keep demanding ID because it is easy.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the Swiss e-ID, the wallet releases only the attribute a transaction needs through selective disclosure; here, the Taiwan digital wallet releases only the single 'female or over threshold' flag to the hotel desk.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A business needs one attribute to proceed, but the credential is issued as a whole, so the holder must rely on the wallet to release only the needed attribute. | mechanism: SD-JWT VC selective disclosure with OpenID4VP presentation and status-list validity check.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the securities foreign-agent rule, a full ID card copy is demanded with no less-intrusive alternative stated; here, the hotel's photocopy habit plays that role and the one-bit credential is the missing alternative.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A foreign investor must prove that its local agent is a real, identified person, and the agent hands over a full copy of an ID card, with no alternative verification stated. | mechanism: None stated; full ID copy required with no less-intrusive alternative given.

title: Rental viewing: 'still employed today' without handing over the ARC and employment contract
moment: A Vietnamese factory worker in Taoyuan views a shared room advertised by a private landlord. To get the deposit discount for 'stable tenants', the landlord asks her to photograph her 居留證 (ARC), passport, employment contract and recent payslip, which he keeps in a LINE chat.
verifier: Individual landlord or sub-letting agent of a shared rental flat near an industrial zone
predicate: Freshness: the holder has a valid employment permit with a named sponsoring employer, issued/refreshed within the last 30 days (not revoked, not expired, not in 'runaway' status)
disclosed_today: Full ARC front and back (ID number, address, permit expiry), passport photo page, whole employment contract with salary and broker name, payslip, often kept indefinitely in a personal LINE/phone gallery
issuer: Ministry of Labor Workforce Development Agency (勞動部勞動力發展署) via the foreign-worker permit system, signing a short-lived employment-status attestation
why_zk: The landlord needs only 'currently permitted to work for an employer' as a basis for trusting rent will be paid; a fresh signed status with a short validity gives that without ID number, salary or contract terms. Honest limit: private landlords have little motivation to adopt a wallet flow, the claim only helps where the tenant has bargaining power via the discount, and the same ARC is still often demanded for the rental-contract filing and registered-residence rules, which would need legal change.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In GDPR data minimisation, a controller is told to take only what the purpose needs but has no way to ask for less than a whole document; here, a freshness-only employment attestation plays the narrower request that the landlord can actually make.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A rule obliges anyone requesting information to take only what the purpose needs, but gives no practical way to request less than a whole document. | mechanism: Legal principle of data minimisation; no technical mechanism specified.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the Google subscription complaint, the service demands an ID and address bill just to confirm payment status and offers no lesser alternative; here, the landlord demanding the ARC, passport and contract to confirm employment status plays that over-collecting service, and the signed status proof plays the missing alternative.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A service needs to confirm a subscriber's payment, but it demands an identity document and address proof, and threatens suspension if the user refuses, without stating the purpose or necessity. | mechanism: None; the complaint notes no stated purpose or less-intrusive alternative was offered.

title: Baseball gate: one-person-one-seat face lane without a face database
moment: At the Taipei Dome on a CPBL game night, the club runs a fast 'face lane' so fans skip the ticket scan. Each fan today enrols a selfie that the club's vendor stores as a template linked to their name and phone, in order to stop ticket resale and duplicate entry. The fan wants to walk in once, show a face, and have nothing kept.
verifier: Professional baseball club's gate operations (stadium operator and its face-gate vendor)
predicate: This credential was issued to exactly one living person, it has not been presented at any gate in this event yet, and the person presenting it now is the one it was issued to (uniqueness: one holder, one entry).
disclosed_today: Selfie and a stored face template, full name, mobile number, ticket ID, seat, and purchase history, kept in the vendor's database after the game for marketing and fraud screening.
issuer: The ticketing platform (e.g. a ticket-sales service) issues the ticket as a credential bound to a device-held key and to a single 'unique person' attestation from a government-recognised digital wallet; the face is matched only against the holder's own device, not against a central template.
why_zk: The gate needs a one-time 'this is the single holder of a valid, unused ticket' proof, which a nullifier-style proof can give without a name, number, or face template; the live face only unlocks the holder's own wallet. Honest limits: the club's resale-fraud worry is real, and the device-side face match is only as strong as the phone's biometrics. The legal pressure to drop templates is weak under the PDPA unless the biometric is treated as special category, so adoption would be driven by liability and trust rather than law.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the Chaum blind-signature ballot scheme, the authority signs a ballot without seeing it and cannot later link it to the signing event; here, the ticketing platform signs a blinded entry token so the gate can verify it without linking it to the buyer's name.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A signer must certify that a holder has a valid token without seeing the token's content, and must later be unable to link the certified token back to the signing event. | mechanism: A blind signature, where the message is blinded with a random factor before signing, and the holder unblinds the signature so it verifies against the original message under the signer's public key.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the Luxembourg tourist rule, the host may inspect the identity document but must not copy it; here, the gate inspects a proof of unique holder and enters the fan but retains no face template or copy.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A host must confirm a visitor's identity and eligibility, but the usual practice is to keep a copy of the whole identity document; the regulator says looking at it is enough. | mechanism: Visual inspection of the identity document with no copy taken; the statutory duty is met by checking, not retaining.

title: Hospital-to-shelter nurse rota: proving current licence without disclosing the employer
moment: A county health bureau asks hospital nurses to take weekend rotations at an earthquake evacuation shelter in Hualien. The shelter's volunteer platform wants confirmation that each rotating nurse is licensed and in good standing this week, and its sign-up form asks for employer, ward, and licence scan. Nurses working in psychiatric or oncology wards, or who work for a rival hospital, do not want their workplace or ward revealed to community volunteers who may be their neighbours or patients' relatives.
verifier: Civil-defence / volunteer-platform operator (county volunteer coordination centre) rostering nurses across shelters
predicate: Licence in good standing as of the last 7 days; employer, ward, and licence number not disclosed
disclosed_today: Licence scan, employer name, department/ward, staff ID, phone and home district, held in a shared volunteer spreadsheet visible to many coordinators
issuer: Taiwan Nurses Association or Ministry of Health and Welfare registry, issuing a weekly renewable licence-status credential; the employing hospital is not involved
why_zk: The sign-up form copies the HIPAA habit of enumerating fields to strip, but leftover fields (ward, district, employer) still re-identify a nurse and her patients' circle; a proof that discloses only licence currency makes the leftover-field judgement unnecessary. Weakness: the platform may still need a contact channel and an emergency contact, and registry-issued weekly credentials require infrastructure the health authority may not provide, so adoption depends on the ministry rather than the volunteer centre.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In HIPAA Safe Harbor, the sharer removes a checklist of identifiers of the individual and relatives or employers yet must still judge residual re-identification; here, the nurse's credential plays that role by disclosing only licence currency so employer and ward never enter the rota and nothing is left to judge.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A party wants to share a record set that cannot identify any person, but the test is a checklist of removable fields plus a no-actual-knowledge condition, so the holder must still judge whether leftover fields re-identify someone. | mechanism: Safe Harbor method removing 18 enumerated identifiers (with ZIP-code truncation rule and age aggregation), or an expert-determination alternative; re-identification codes allowed only if not derived from or disclosed about the individual.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In jury selection, names of those seated may be published by default with confidentiality only as a judge-level exception; here, the volunteer rota's default of listing employer and ward plays that role and the credential makes confidentiality the default instead of an exception granted per nurse.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: Someone must be drawn from a pool and seated for a task without the wider public learning who they are, but the default rule can flip to full publication of the identities of everyone selected, with confidentiality only as a judge-level exception. | mechanism: Judge-discretionary confidentiality of juror names under a court's jury selection plan; no technical mechanism specified.

title: Landlord-assisted room-share: sealed check done by the community, shown to a new flatmate
moment: A tenant in a Kaohsiung student apartment block wants to sublet one room to a stranger from a Facebook housing group. The previous flatmates insist that whoever moves in has been checked, but nobody wants to read another person's whole record or learn why a past record exists. A neighbourhood community management committee can do a one-off check.
verifier: The sitting tenants of the flat deciding on a sublet applicant, relying on the committee's signature
predicate: Applicant is not on the violent-offender list at the committee's check time, with the result kept hidden from everyone but the holder until the holder chooses to present it on move-in day
disclosed_today: Photocopy of the applicant's ID and 良民證, handed to the tenants and the community committee, with the committee office keeping a copy in its files
issuer: The community management committee (社區管理委員會) or a licensed housing agency, who obtains the applicant's own consented record query and signs a short-lived non-membership attestation
why_zk: Today the committee office holds copies of strangers' records that it has no reason to keep; a sealed attestation that the holder reveals only at move-in cuts that retention and stops the flatmates seeing record details. Weakness: a community committee is not an obviously trusted authority for criminal checks, and the legal permission to run such a check on behalf of private persons is unclear in Taiwan, so this idea is the weakest of the three.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In an-b-sealed-bid-far, the holder of sealed bids keeps them unopened until the scheduled moment and may handle the envelope only to identify it; here, the committee plays the holder who may confirm the attestation's identity and validity without opening the underlying record.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A party submits a value that must stay hidden from competitors until a fixed moment, while the holder of the submissions must be able to prove later that none were seen early and must handle identifying wrappers without exposing the content. | mechanism: Physical and access-control safeguarding of sealed bids with designated-official exception for envelope identification, plus a written record of any mistaken early opening.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In an-b-jury-selection, a court keeps selected people's names confidential only as a judge-level exception to a default of publication; here, the committee's rule that the check result stays with the holder by default plays that protection, rather than relying on the committee's discretion to withhold.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: Someone must be drawn from a pool and seated for a task without the wider public learning who they are, but the default rule can flip to full publication of the identities of everyone selected, with confidentiality only as a judge-level exception. | mechanism: Judge-discretionary confidentiality of juror names under a court's jury selection plan; no technical mechanism specified.
